thread:
maya: Heads-up: ap-southeast1 canary is showing node-level OOMs + driver kmod errors after the GPU driver rollout wave 2.
nico: saw that. Which driver version did the canary get? logs?
sre-oncall: deploy-bot flagged the rollout and auto-canary policy. Here's the event + snippet from node: 
```
Mar 25 03:12:04 host kernel: nvidia: module licensing mismatch
Mar 25 03:12:04 host kernel: nvidia: init_module failed: -22
Mar 25 03:12:07 host dockerd: Container exited with code 137 (OOM)
```
maya: nodes were upgraded to driver 535.54.03 but kernel modules report 535.35.02 still loaded. suspect kmod/driver package drift during reboot window.
nico: that explains NCCL hangs we saw in the canary pods. If module ABI mismatch -> nv_peer_mem/KVM issues and stalls.
kai: can we isolate to a subset of pool? how many dedicated racks affected?
maya: 4/24 dedicated racks in ap-southeast1 due to staggered wave. Only affects capacity-tagged nodes running dedicated-rt pool.
sre-oncall: immediate action: pause the remaining waves in ap-southeast1 and ap-south1. rollback plan or rebind kmod? options:
- option A: force re-install older driver 535.35.02 and reboot nodes (impact: node restarts, evict pods)
- option B: reload kmod with the new package (risky if package mismatch persists)
- option C: taint affected nodes and failover to fallback region until patch applied
nico: prefer A for safety; consistent package + reboot avoids half-baked kernels. we'll schedule rolling reboots with drain.
deploy-bot: rollout:driver/535.54.03 -> paused by @sre-oncall at 2026-03-25T03:18:02Z :warning:
ops-comm: if we restart nodes we'll need an external comms timeline for Dedicated customers (SLA note). Can we limit restarts to non-reserved racks first?
maya: yes, we can sequence non-reserved racks first. patch will target nodepool label: gpu.dedicated=false then escalate.
nico: commands i'm running to detect remaining mismatches:
```
# on node
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv
modinfo nvidia | grep version
uname -r
```
maya: sample output from node-07: `driver_version, 535.54.03` vs `modinfo: version: 535.35.02` -> mismatch
sre-oncall: I'll create a one-off maintenance window: ap-southeast1 03:40-04:40 UTC. plan: cordon+drain -> install 535.35.02 package -> reboot -> uncordon. We'll mirror to remaining racks after validation.
kai: can we automate detection and tainting? want to avoid manual misses.
nico: yes i'll add a short sweep script that checks `modinfo` vs package manifest and labels nodes with `gpu.driver_mismatch=true` if mismatch.
ops-comm: timeline for customer heads-up? email and console banner?
maya: draft message: "We observed a driver mismatch affecting a subset of Dedicated GPUs in ap-southeast1. We're performing a targeted maintenance window; some workloads may be evicted briefly. No data loss expected. ETA 60 minutes." comment?
ops-comm: add SLA impact: "may see degraded throughput in dedicated pools for up to 1 hour; team on-call will prioritize rollback if regressions persist." include contact for urgent customer issues.
sre-oncall: after patching first 2 racks metrics look stable, NCCL allreduce latency back to baseline. keeping remaining racks paused pending overnight soak.
maya: next steps: 1) sweep script merged to infra repo 2) run drain+install on non-reserved racks 3) schedule reserved racks during low-usage window 4) post-mortem to capture root cause (package repo race or image bake timing)
nico: I'll open a PR for the sweep + a follow-up playbook snippet for driver rollbacks. includes commands and how to revert: 
```
# rollback command example
kubectl label nodes node-07 gpu.rollout-paused=true
apt-get install nvidia-driver-535=535.35.02-1 && reboot
```
maya: thanks. big +1 on adding automatic tainting so future waves stop early if kmod mismatch detected.
deploy-bot: canary:driver-checker reported 6 nodes with mismatch and auto-paused wave at 03:22 UTC :white_check_mark:
ops-comm: i'll prepare the customer-facing note and post in #dedicated-status. we should also update the status API with affected region tag.
maya: filing the incident ticket and scheduling a postmortem with eng-infra + eng-runtime + buildfarm (possible packaging race). will include timeline and cost impact estimate (failed jobs + evictions).
